acceptance: A test inside a lane cell (the build floor of a cycle) lists the process table and reads the command of one pid through proctree with no exec of ps, red before the change
The darwin and linux readers return the same pid, ppid, pgid and comm as ps for the test process and its parent
go test -count=1 ./internal/faketmux passes inside a lane cell after faketmux moves to the new reader
fix: Design first (protected path; design review before build). Candidate: export a per-pid reader (for example proctree.ArgsOf(pid)) that wraps readProcArgs, and a ps-free table lister (sysctl KERN_PROC_ALL on darwin, a /proc scan on linux) that returns pid, ppid, pgid and comm, behind the existing Lister seam. List every caller of NewLister/ExecLister and decide whether each moves to the ps-free lister. Then faketmux-reaper-needs-no-ps-binary builds on it.
summary: A console-builder run on 2026-11-19 (agent-console-builder-20261119T125612Z-7945) for faketmux-reaper-needs-no-ps-binary found the blocker in go/internal/proctree: NewLister and ExecLister run `ps -A -o pid=,ppid=,pgid=,uid=,lstart=,comm=` through sysexec (list.go), and the per-pid readers readProcArgs (procargs_darwin.go, procargs_linux.go) and readProcStart are unexported. ArgsReader is an exported type with no exported implementation. A lane cell denies ps ('fork/exec /bin/ps: operation not permitted'), so faketmux (session.go:31 commandOf, format.go:80 runPS) and every caller of the proctree listers fail inside a cell. 8 faketmux tests are red in every lane cell.
title: proctree reads the process table through ps, which a lane cell denies, and exports no ps-free reader
